title: Results Ledger
read_first: None of these results has been peer reviewed. They are preprints by one independent author, produced with disclosed AI assistance.
"Lean kernel" means the Lean 4 kernel accepted the proof. That certifies the formal statement, not the choice of statement, so every result also records a statement audit.

The audit recorded for each result was run by AI review agents in sessions separate from the ones that wrote the proofs, under the author's direction: a clean rebuild at the cited commit, a reading of the formal statement against the claim and its cited source, and a literature search. It is an internal check, not external review.
A result answers only the question stated. Parent problems named in the papers remain open unless they are listed here.
not_claimed: No Millennium Prize problem and no grand open problem is solved here. P versus NP is open.
No result has been refereed by a journal or checked by a named outside expert.
Engineering invariant suites (section F) verify software models. They are not evidence about consciousness, sentience, biology or physics.
A search that found no earlier proof is not a proof of novelty.
admission_rules: The claim is registered in the archive with a pinned commit and a frozen paper.
The formal statement is read against the informal claim and against the cited source, in a session that did not write the proof.
The proof is rebuilt from a clean clone at that commit, or the ledger says it was not.
The literature is searched for earlier or parallel proofs and the outcome is recorded.
The wording is limited to what steps 2 to 4 support. Anything narrower than the usual informal claim is stated under Limit.
challenge: Open an issue on this repository or on the result's repository and quote the result number (for example R7).
A reproducible counterexample, a gap in a statement audit, or an earlier proof in the literature leads to a correction: the result is narrowed, reclassified or withdrawn, and keeps its number.

results.title: Digit-sum characterisation of two-register passive register programs with F_p constants
results.statement: For p prime, t ≥ 1, f ∈ F_p[x]: a passive two-register program (instructions O += P(R), R += c, O += λx, R += λx; constants in F_p) with at most t input accesses producing O + f(x) and restoring R, as an identity of formal polynomials in F_p[R, x], exists exactly when every d ≥ 2 with [x^d]f ≠ 0 has base-p digit sum s_p(d) ≤ min(p−1, t−1).
results.evidence_note: Formal identity implies correct execution in every commutative ring of characteristic p (proved, T1s); the converse step is a paper argument.
limits: Cleanliness means equality of formal polynomials; as functions on F_p itself x^p = x, so for example x^3 over F_2 is computed with one input access although the theorem excludes it.
Program constants lie in the prime field; with F_4 constants the criterion changes (x^3 becomes computable), and the case of general F_(p^e) is open.

Vinciguerra (arXiv:2609.18692) proves the characteristic-0 analogue (Theorem 3.5) and does not pose the positive-characteristic question; this is a self-posed extension, not an answer to a published question.
Two registers only; nothing is shown for three or more registers in positive characteristic.
That literal clean execution over a polynomial ring implies the formal predicate (needed to read the 'only if' half as a statement about executions) is not formalised.
Prior-work search was limited to arXiv, Semantic Scholar and one web query on 2026-11-26.

results.title: Two-access programs for x^(2^k) in characteristic 2 using product updates only
results.statement: For k ≥ 1 and every commutative ring with 2 = 0, a program on k+1 registers with instructions R_d += R_a·R_b (d ∉ {a, b}; register 0 never read) and R_d += x uses 2 input accesses and 4k−2 products, adds x^(2^k) to register 0 and restores the others, from every initial state. With k+2 registers and copies R_d += R_s, the indices d, a, b are pairwise distinct.
results.evidence_note: Elementary: repeated squaring with (a+b)² = a² + b² in characteristic 2.
limits: Characteristic 2 only.
No lower bound on registers, products or input accesses is proved.
The product-only instruction set is the repository's restriction of the register-program model; the statement is not tied to a published question.
Only general searches of the register-program literature were run; the underlying identity is standard.

results.title: Four-register passive powering of x^N with fewer than (104/3)·N^(log₁₃ 8) input accesses
results.statement: Let N ≥ 1 have ℓ+1 base-13 digits. Over every commutative ring in which D_8 = 2656207148788801777680, 12! and (ℓ+1)! are invertible, some passive four-register program maps (o, u, r₁, r₂) to (o + x^N, u, r₁, r₂) with fewer than (104/3)·8^ℓ ≤ (104/3)·N^(log₁₃ 8) input accesses. Counting ℓ+1 base-7 digits instead: 6! and (ℓ+1)! invertible, fewer than (70/3)·5^ℓ accesses. The base-13 bound is also stated coordinatewise over Rⁿ.
results.evidence_note: Lean states 3·accesses < 104·8^ℓ with 13^ℓ ≤ N; the real-exponent form and the comparison with log₅ 4 are paper-level conversions.
limits: Improves the exponent of Corollary 4.3.1 of arXiv:2609.18692 at four registers (log₅ 4 ≈ 0.8614 to log₁₃ 8 ≈ 0.8107); with the stated constants the bound is smaller than 20·N^(log₅ 4) only for N above about 52,000 (base-7 variant: above about 90).

No lower bound is proved: log₁₃ 8 is the smallest exponent among the constructed base programs (t = 8 minimises log_(2t−3) t over integers t ≥ 4, which is integer arithmetic), not a proven optimum for three-register base programs.
In prime characteristic p the hypotheses exclude p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 137, 1602207194491} and require p > ℓ+1, which limits N.
With five registers the cited paper already has the smaller exponent log₇ 4 ≈ 0.712.
The coordinatewise corollary contains no stream model or space bound; the streaming and matrix-powering applications are paper arguments outside Lean.

results.title: Lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of the odd cycles C₂₅ and C₂₉
results.statement: C₂₅^⊠144 contains an independent set of size M with 12344196091426841^144 ≤ M·10^(15·144), and C₂₉^⊠4 contains an independent set of size 42050, where 14319949949077991^4 ≤ 42050·10^60. Consequently Θ(C₂₅) ≥ 12.344196091426841 and Θ(C₂₉) ≥ 14.319949949077991. Both exceed the largest earlier values found, 23125^(1/4) ≈ 12.3316 and 42017^(1/4) ≈ 14.3171 (Codenotti–Gerace–Resta 2003, Table 1).
results.evidence_note: Θ is not defined in Lean; the capacity bounds follow from the integer statements by Θ(G) = sup α(G^⊠d)^(1/d).
limits: Lower bounds only; the exact value of Θ(C_n) is open for every odd n ≥ 7.
The margins over the 2003 values are 0.01257 (C₂₅) and 0.00281 (C₂₉, 33 more words in the fourth power), smaller than the gains the repository states against third-power values.
The C₂₅ base set has the 2003 published size 23125; the gain comes from a port system and the Buys–Polak–Zuiddam substitution tables, whose framework this follows.
The prior-work search was not exhaustive: Baumert et al. 1971 and Hales 1973 were not opened, and the 2003 table entries are printed cardinalities.

results.title: Independent sets in the fourth strong power of C_n for n = 4m+1
results.statement: For every m ≥ 5 with m ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4) and n = 4m+1: α(C_n^⊠4) ≥ (m² + ⌊m/4⌋)·n². The set is lifted from m² + ⌊m/4⌋ = ⌊n⌊n/4⌋/4⌋ points of ℤ_n², no two within circular distance 3 in both coordinates; no such point set is larger (n ≥ 4), and each one of size M lifts to M·n² points (n ≥ 9).
results.evidence_note: Three contract theorems: lifting (T1a), ceiling (T1b), family (T1d).
limits: For m ≡ 0 (mod 4), n = 16j+1, the size equals (n⁴−n³)/16, the exact value of α(C_n^⊠4) credited to Baumert et al. (1971) in the 2003 paper of Codenotti, Gerace and Resta.
The case n = 21 (11466 words, 26 cosets of ⟨(1,0,0,2),(0,1,2,0)⟩) is in the 2026 Lean repository of Buys, Polak and Zuiddam.
For m ≡ 1 (mod 4), m ≥ 9, the sizes exceed the 2003 table entries at n = 37 and n = 53 (113627 vs 113586, 483148 vs 483091); no search for later work on these n was done.
The ceiling bounds unions of cosets of one subgroup, not α(C_n^⊠4); Lean proves the lifting direction only.

results.title: Frozen bit strings of the 0110↔1001 dipole-conserving gate
results.statement: Swapping 0110 and 1001 preserves charge and dipole moment. The sequence Z with Z(0..4) = 1, 2, 4, 8, 14 and Z(L) = Z(L−1) + Z(L−2) + Z(L−4) for L ≥ 5 equals the number of length-L bit strings avoiding 0110 and 1001 for L = 1, …, 6, and satisfies 2Z(L) < Z(L+4) for L ≥ 1. Over ℤ, x⁴ − x³ − x² − 1 = (x+1)(x³ − 2x² + x − 1).
results.evidence_note: Count identity kernel-checked for L ≤ 6 only; agreement for larger L is computational (L ≤ 14 in the repository, L ≤ 15 in this audit).
limits: The 'Plastic-constant-squared' conjunct is vacuous: ρ³ = ρ + 1 has no integer solution.
The growth rate ρ² and Θ(ρ^(2L)) are not in Lean.
'Skin-effect immunity' of frozen strings follows directly from the definition of frozen.

The string count is kernel-checked only for L = 1, …, 6. dfa_total_eq_zFrozen proves the recurrence for a four-state transfer count for every L, but that count is never proved equal to the number of bit strings.

The counting sequence coincides with OEIS A164394 (stated there for the pattern pair 0001, 0100) on L = 0..15; exponentially many frozen states under dipole-conserving dynamics are known (Sala et al. 2020; Khemani et al. 2020).

results.title: Algebraic closed forms of the Banić–Elezović recombination expressions for γ(n), γ_c(n), γ(3;N), γ(4;N)
results.statement: With p₁ = (n²−4n−4)/(32πn), q₁ = a_△·n/π − (n+1)/(8πn), r₁ = −(n+1)/(8πn) and a_△ = 1/32 − 4√3/243: for real n ≠ 0, (n−1)p₁ + 2(n−2)q₁ + (n−2)(n−3)r₁ = −n(n+1)/(32π) − 8√3·n(n−2)/(243π) + (n−1)/(8πn), and n·p₁ + 2n·q₁ + n(n−3)r₁ = −n(n+4)/(32π) − 8√3·n²/(243π). Two analogous identities hold at n = 3 and n = 4.
results.evidence_note: Identities between real numbers only. That the left sides are variance coefficients is taken from Banić–Elezović, outside Lean.

results.title: ML-KEM parameter arithmetic and a Compress_1 decoding margin
results.statement: 3329 is prime and 17 has multiplicative order 256 modulo 3329; signed Montgomery reduction returns r with r·2^16 ≡ a (mod 3329) and |r| < 3329 for |a| < 2^15·3329; for b ∈ {0,1} and |e| ≤ 831 the repository's Lean function mlkemCompress1 maps b·1665 + e to b.

limits: The Lean Compress_1 model is not FIPS 203: it returns 1 at x = 832 where FIPS 203 returns 0.
The companion claim that both b = 0 and b = 1 fail at e = +832 (adv_compress1_fails_at_plus_832, the CI negative test, the paper) is false for FIPS 203; only b = 1 fails.
